language_wrapper: A {dimension}-dimensional axis-aligned rectangular box is assembled from 1-by-...-1 unit hypercubes, with integer side lengths [side_lengths]. Consider the straight space-diagonal segment from one corner to the opposite corner. Through the interiors of how many unit hypercubes does this segment pass?
hardness_rationale: The seed problem uses the 3D formula N = a + b + c − gcd(a, b) − gcd(b, c) − gcd(c, a) + gcd(a, b, c). Our family elevates the task to d ≥ 4 dimensions with integer side lengths chosen to force multiple distinct pairwise gcds and at least one nontrivial triple gcd. Solving requires recognizing and applying the full higher-dimensional inclusion–exclusion formula N = Σ a_i − Σ gcd(a_i, a_j) + Σ gcd(a_i, a_j, a_k) − … + (−1)^{d−1} gcd(a_1, …, a_d), together with careful bookkeeping over all subsets. The verifier enforces that instances cannot be reduced to pairwise-coprime cases or simple patterns, ensuring the solution genuinely demands higher-order reasoning beyond the 3D seed.
notes: Proof sketch of correctness: Consider the segment from the origin to (a_1, …, a_d) in ℝ^d with axis-aligned unit hypercube tiling. Each time the segment crosses an integer hyperplane x_i = m (for some i and integer m ∈ {1, 2, …, a_i − 1}), it enters a new hypercube along direction i, contributing a_i − 1 events per coordinate. Summing gives Σ_i (a_i − 1), but this double-counts whenever the segment hits multiple coordinate hyperplanes simultaneously. Such simultaneous hits occur precisely when the parameter t along the segment makes all relevant coordinates integers at once, i.e., when t is a rational with denominator dividing gcd of the corresponding subset of side lengths. The count of simultaneous crossings for a subset S of coordinates equals gcd({a_i : i ∈ S}) − 1. Inclusion–exclusion over all nonempty subsets S yields the exact number of distinct hypercubes entered: Σ_i (a_i − 1) − Σ_{|S|=2} (gcd(S) − 1) + Σ_{|S|=3} (gcd(S) − 1) − … + (−1)^{d−1} (gcd(all) − 1). Rearranging the alternating sum of the constant 1 terms gives the compact formula N = Σ a_i − Σ gcd(a_i, a_j) + Σ gcd(a_i, a_j, a_k) − … + (−1)^{d−1} gcd(a_1, …, a_d). This generalizes the well-known 2D and 3D results and matches the combinatorial behavior of boundary crossings. The generator ensures rich gcd structure (distinct pairwise gcds and a nontrivial triple gcd) with overall gcd 1, so higher-order inclusion–exclusion terms are essential and the instance is nontrivial.
source_question: A $150\times 324\times 375$ rectangular solid is made by gluing together $1\times 1\times 1$ cubes. An internal diagonal of this solid passes through the interiors of how many of the $1\times 1\times 1$ cubes?
